multipleChoice.question: What has research suggested about knowing more than one language?
options: It may affect the brain and bring health benefits.
It makes people speak faster in every language.
It prevents children from learning their first language.
It removes the need for formal education.

multipleChoice.question: What do babies in multilingual environments need to do?
options: Choose one language and stop hearing the others.
Listen carefully to the languages around them.
Speak all languages before they understand them.
Learn grammar rules before they can communicate.

multipleChoice.question: What skill do multilingual children practise when speaking?
options: Translating every word into their mother tongue.
Focusing on one language while setting another aside.
Using the same language with every person.
Avoiding difficult conversations.

multipleChoice.question: What difference is mentioned between bilinguals and monolinguals with dementia?
options: Bilinguals may show symptoms later.
Monolinguals never develop symptoms.
Bilinguals recover more quickly.
Monolinguals forget all languages first.

multipleChoice.question: Why is juggling several languages compared to a brain workout?
options: It may make the brain work more efficiently.
It is physically tiring like sports training.
It requires people to avoid using their first language.
It works only for people who start as babies.

multipleChoice.question: How did Neil’s motivation for language learning change later in life?
options: He became more motivated when he worked abroad.
He stopped learning because languages were too difficult.
He found school language lessons more useful than work.
He learned languages mainly to pass university exams.

multipleChoice.question: How was Hannah’s experience different from Neil’s?
options: She found languages easier at school and university.
She learned languages only after moving abroad.
She avoided learning languages until adulthood.
She learned languages because her job required it.

multipleChoice.question: Why did Victoria learn several languages?
options: Her family moved between different countries.
She wanted to become a language teacher.
Her school required eight official languages.
She studied them all at university.

multipleChoice.question: Why did Victoria’s parents continue learning Norwegian even though it was hard?
options: They needed it to work and live in Norway.
Their children refused to speak their mother tongue.
They wanted to become professional translators.
They already knew many European languages.

multipleChoice.question: What advice does Victoria give for learning a language?
options: Surround yourself with real examples of the language.
Memorise grammar before listening to people.
Avoid public places until you speak perfectly.
Learn only through online lessons.
